context.title: The Queen of Heaven
context.summary: Jeremiah confronts the Judeans living across Egypt, who have seen Jerusalem's ruin yet still burn incense to other gods. They answer that life was better when they honored the 'queen of heaven,' and Jeremiah announces that only a few will return, with Pharaoh Hophra's fall as a sign.
context.background: Judeans had settled from Migdol and Tahpanhes in the north to Pathros, Upper Egypt (v. 1). Papyri from Elephantine, an island in Upper Egypt, later show a Jewish community with its own temple there in the 400s BC. Pharaoh Hophra (Apries) was overthrown by his general Amasis around 570 BC and later killed.

customs.note: Baked cakes, perhaps shaped in the goddess's image, offered with drink offerings. The women add that their husbands approved.

watchFor: The people argue from experience: when we worshiped her, 'we… were well' (vv. 17–18).
'Whose words shall stand, mine, or theirs' (v. 28).

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth (Jer. 1:1; 32:6). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628).

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.summary: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: The last king of Judah. He was the third son of Josiah, and his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, and hence he was the brother of Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31; 24:17, 18).

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Memphis
places.summary: Only in Hos. 9:6, Hebrew Moph. In Isa. 19:13; Jer. 2:16; 46:14, 19; Ezek. 30:13, 16, it is mentioned under the name Noph. It was the capital of Lower, i.e., of Northern Egypt.

places.name: Migdol
places.summary: A strongly-fortified place 12 miles from Pelusium, in the north of Egypt (Jer. 44:1; 46:14).

places.name: Pathros
places.summary: The name generally given to Upper Egypt (the Thebaid of the Greeks), as distinguished from Matsor, or Lower Egypt (Isa. 11:11; Jer. 44:1, 15; Ezek. 30:14), the two forming Mizraim.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

events.title: Prophecies of Jeremiah
events.summary: Passage: Jeremiah 1:1–52:34. People: Jeremiah. Lasted about 67 years.
